King Muhammad bin Nayef stood proudly on stage, a few index cards in his hand. "Today I have an important announcement to make, one that will effect Saudi Arabia like nothing before.

It had been my original intention to announce the integration of women into Saudi Arabian research teams, however the Committee for the Promotion of Virtue and Prevention of Vice raised concern with this, complaining it would make it impossible for them to do their job. After extended talks and what I consider to be fair compromise, I am excited to announce the first all-woman Saudi Arabian research team, here in Riyadh.

These women will work both indirectly alongside male research teams, as well as tackle their own projects. In instances where men and women researchers are working on the same projects, data will be submitted to a project lead electronically and without any knowledge of which data came from which group.

For years many women in Saudi Arabia have held degrees, have had knowledge that could be pushing our nation forward. Women make up a majority of college graduates in Saudi Arabia. Yet, until now we have not allowed women to do much other than teach. While spreading knowledge to the next generation is integral to the future of Saudi Arabia, if Allah has gifted a woman with an understanding of science, we should let that gift shine."
